prompt: Create a polished, high-fidelity native iPhone application UI mockup, a single portrait screen filling the image (approximately 393 x 852 point aspect ratio), NOT a poster, NOT a phone hardware rendering, no device bezel, no side-by-side screens. This is the first screen of a NEW app called "Pulse" for live heart rate from a Garmin sensor. The app contains ONLY pulse-related content, no notification tooling, logs, QR codes, debugger, account, marketing, claims, gamification scores, ECG waveform, medical advice, health zones or fake calories. All measurement content is synthetic and visibly labeled "Demo · Sample data". This is a calm but highly expressive kinetic-mobile visual world: matte plum, lavender and pale lilac-pink surfaces, crisp precise large San Francisco-style native numerals, ordinary SF native labels, unusually beautiful flat elliptical ribbons as an abstract moving pulse sculpture, no gradients, no glowing neon, no glass cards. This abstract sculpture is an animation based on reported rate, NOT a heart diagram or actual ECG. Native iPhone safe-area spacing, status bar at top (9:41), home indicator at bottom, familiar native toolbar with "Pulse" title and a small watch connection button. Design minimum 44pt tap targets and clear contrast. A single central artistic moment, disciplined supporting content, no generic card grid. Readable exact UI copy. The viewport must look like a finished app ready to implement in SwiftUI. COMPOSITION OPTION 2 — PULSE AND RECENT TREND. Same palette and world, but composition materially differs: pale lilac page, native toolbar, upper horizontal section with large plum "72" and "BPM" aligned left, and a smaller crop of the kinetic ellipse sculpture floating on the right; generous whitespace, not a card. Middle 35 percent becomes one beautiful continuous plum-colored field containing the lilac sculpture moving across it horizontally; no giant heart icon. Lower third shows a real-looking sample pulse trend line, NOT ECG, labeled "Last 60 seconds" with faint readable axes "60s ago" and "Now"; smooth small variation from 68 to 78, no jagged ECG spikes. Under it simple typography "68 low" and "78 high". A bottom native button "Choose watch". Explicit readable "Demo · Sample data" visible. The art, number and actual chart have distinct roles, no additional metrics, no generic tiles. Compose for 393 x 852 portrait.
note: Synthetic sample data; design mockup, not running app.
